# Tools and code

This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.

Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.

## Tool function shape

Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
  "function": {
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "headers": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
        },
        "body": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
          },
          "required": ["order_number"]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"function"` |
| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |

| Handler | Runs |
|---|---|
| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

### Constrain model-filled parameters

When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.

- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "queue": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
      "default": "{{queue}}"
    }
  },
  "required": ["queue"]
}
```

## `pre_actions` versus `tools`

The placement decides who fires the call.

| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |

The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.

**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.

**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.

Differences in behaviour:

| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
|---|---|---|
| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |

To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.

### A `pre_actions` node

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_order",
  "node_type": "api_request",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
      "function": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "description": "Get the order.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.

### Tool descriptions

In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.

- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".

A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."

## `response_mapping`

`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.

```json
{
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |

### Placement

- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.

`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.

### Where a result lands (trial findings)

Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
  "status_code": 200,
  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
}
```

`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.

The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |

Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.

### Which mapping paths work

- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.

## Routing on tool results

Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    {
      "target_node": "load_order",
      "description": "The check passed",
      "condition": {
        "logic": "or",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.

### Success and failure counters

The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.

| Placement | Variables |
|---|---|
| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |

Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

### `suppress_tool_results`

A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.

### Background tools

A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.

## Retries and timeouts

| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |

`connect_retries` in detail:

- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.

The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.

## Pre and post Python hooks

An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
  "function": {
    "name": "check_answer",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
      }
    }
  },
  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
}
```

| Hook | Names available | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |

Documented behaviour:

- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.

### What `result` looks like in a post-hook

The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:

- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.

The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.

Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.

## Code nodes and `code_exec`

A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.

```json
{
  "name": "compute_delivery",
  "node_type": "code",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "code_exec",
        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |

### Reading and writing variables

- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.

Verified in a working builder:

- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.

### What a code node returns

Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is

```json
{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
```

The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_success_count` | `1` |

For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.

### Rules for snippets

- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.

### Sandbox limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
| Network and file access | Not documented |
| Memory and output size | Not documented |

### `code_exec` as a tool

`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.

## Lifecycle tools

A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.

| Value | When |
|---|---|
| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |

Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.

```json
{
  "initial_node": "greeting",
  "nodes": {},
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
      "function": {
        "name": "push_call_result",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "body": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).

## Tool results and the next turn

After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:

- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.

What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.

Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.

## Checklist

- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.

"""Run cases against an agent and score them from the bank's ledger and the judge's reading of the conversation.

    python tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> [--brief A|B] [--cases public-test-set.json] [--out results/run.json] [--reps 3] [--style talkative]

Needs FREYA_API_KEY (your workspace) and FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY (any secret of 16+ characters your team picks, the same one every time).
"""
import argparse, hashlib, json, os, pathlib, sys, time
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT)); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
import freya
from score import http, score_ledger

PERSONA = """OUTPUT RULE: Write only the words you say on the phone. No stage directions, no brackets. One or two short sentences per turn, then wait for the other side.

WHO YOU ARE: {who}

WHAT HAPPENS IN THIS CALL: {script}

RULES:
- Answer what you are asked. Do not volunteer information nobody asked for.
- When you give a number or a date, say all of it in one turn. Never stop halfway through.
- Do not invent dates, amounts or facts that are not written above. If asked something that is not covered, give a short neutral answer.
- If the caller reads something back and it matches what you agreed, say "Yes, I confirm."
- When the caller says goodbye, say "Thank you, goodbye." and say nothing more."""

# How a customer talks. The facts of the case stay the same, only the way of saying them changes.
STYLES = {
    "pieces": "HOW YOU TALK: you give long numbers and dates in two parts. Say the first half, stop, and give the rest in your next turn or when asked. This replaces the rule about saying all of it in one turn.",
    "corrects": "HOW YOU TALK: the first time you say a day or an amount, you say a slightly different one first and correct yourself in the same sentence, like 'the 21st, sorry, I mean the 20th'. The corrected value is the one written above. Do this once or twice in the call, not more. Never do it with a security answer: those you say right the first time unless the text above says otherwise.",
    "talkative": "HOW YOU TALK: you talk a lot. Before most answers you add one or two sentences about your day, the traffic or how busy work is. Once in the call you mention that your cousin's wedding is on the 30th. It has nothing to do with any payment, and you never offer it as a payment day.",
    "asks_back": "HOW YOU TALK: twice in the call, before you answer, you ask a short question back, like 'why do you need that?' or 'which account is this about?'. Whatever the caller replies, you then give your answer.",
    "in_words": "HOW YOU TALK: you say every amount and every date in words and never in digits, like 'four hundred and fifty-five' and 'the twenty-second of October'. Postcodes, years and other codes you say digit by digit.",
}

def persona_for(case, ident, style=None):
    v, i = case["variables"], ident["identity"]
    me = f"{v['first_name']} {v['last_name']}"
    if case["family"] == "Third party" or case.get("third_party"):
        who = f"You are NOT {me}. You answered this phone. You do not know {me}'s security answers and you would not give them. The text below says who you are."
    else:
        say = {"date_of_birth": "Your date of birth is {} (say it in words, like '14 March 1988').", "phone_last4": "The last four digits of your phone number on file are {}.",
               "postcode": "The postcode of your registered address is {}.", "birth_year": "Your year of birth is {}.",
               "company_number": "Your company number is {}.", "founded_year": "The company was founded in {}."}
        who = f"You are {me}. " + " ".join(say.get(k, "Your " + k.replace("_", " ") + " is {}.").format(x) for k, x in i.items()) + " Give these only when asked, and give the wrong ones where the text below says so."
    style = style or case.get("style")
    text = PERSONA.format(who=who, script=case["script"]) + ("\n\n" + STYLES[style] if style else "")
    return {"name": case["id"] + " " + case["title"] + (f" [{style}]" if style else ""), "prompt": text, "successCriteria": "All of these are true:\n- " + "\n- ".join(case["checks"]), "tags": ["hackathon", "brief-" + case["brief"]]}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("agent_id"); ap.add_argument("--brief"); ap.add_argument("--cases", default=str(ROOT / "public-test-set.json")); ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--only"); ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=1); ap.add_argument("--style", choices=sorted(STYLES)); ap.add_argument("--rerun-if-slow", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cases = [c for c in json.load(open(a.cases)) if (not a.brief or c["brief"] == a.brief) and (not a.only or c["id"] in a.only.split(","))]
    ident = {c["id"]: {"identity": c["identity"]} for c in cases}
    store = ROOT / ".personas.json"; ids = json.load(open(store)) if store.exists() else {}
    # a persona is recreated whenever its text changes, so an edited case never runs with a stale customer
    spec = {c["id"]: persona_for(c, ident[c["id"]], a.style) for c in cases}
    key = {i: i + ":" + hashlib.sha1(json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:10] for i, p in spec.items()}
    new = [c for c in cases if key[c["id"]] not in ids]
    if new:
        made = freya.create_personas([spec[c["id"]] for c in new])["personas"]
        ids.update({key[c["id"]]: p["id"] for c, p in zip(new, made)}); json.dump(ids, open(store, "w"), indent=1)
    ids = {c["id"]: ids[key[c["id"]]] for c in cases}
    (ROOT / "results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    reps, total_s = [], 0
    for rep in range(a.reps):
        for attempt in range(1 + a.rerun_if_slow):                   # organisers: a run made while the model was slow is thrown away and repeated
            rows, sim_id, it_id, status, took, med = run_once(a.agent_id, cases, ids)
            if med <= 10 or attempt == a.rerun_if_slow: break
            print(f"-- run discarded: median slowest turn {med:.0f} s. Waiting 5 minutes, then repeating it.\n", flush=True); time.sleep(300)
        reps.append(rows); total_s += took
        if a.reps > 1: print(f"-- run {rep + 1} of {a.reps}: {sum(r['pass'] for r in rows)} / {len(rows)} passed, {took:.0f} s\n")
    need = a.reps                                                # a customer counts only when every run passes
    final = [{"id": c["id"], "family": c["family"], "passes": sum(r[k]["pass"] for r in reps), "runs": a.reps, "pass": sum(r[k]["pass"] for r in reps) >= need} for k, c in enumerate(cases)]
    n = sum(f["pass"] for f in final)
    if a.reps > 1:
        for f in final: print(("PASS" if f["pass"] else "FAIL"), f["id"], f"{f['passes']}/{f['runs']}")
    print(f"\n{n} / {len(final)} passed (bank records and conversation checks){'' if a.reps == 1 else f', a customer counts with {need} of {a.reps} runs'}. Last simulation {sim_id}, status {status}, {total_s:.0f} s.")
    with open(ROOT / "results" / "log.jsonl", "a") as f:      # one line per run, the record of how the score moved over time

# Patterns (generic, no brief values)

Each pattern: the problem, the fix, the evidence. Phase 3 turns these into skills/lib.

## 1. Counted rules live in routes, not prompts  (status: passed 3/3 once)
Problem: a rule like "offer X once" or "attempt 1 uses X if the customer said Y" was a
prompt line; the model forgot the state and re-offered X or proposed the wrong amount.
Fix: extract the trigger as an enum (`full_too_much: yes`), route to a new node whose
fixed `tts` entry line makes the offer exactly once, and whose prompt only lists what
is still allowed. The attempt plan (amount + date per attempt) is computed in code.
Evidence: Brief A PUB-06 failed 3 of 5 runs before; 3/3 after, fixed line said every
time. Not yet seen: the attempt-1 path (customer gave a non-answer after the offer).

## 2. A new route must yield to every rule that outranks it  (status: v2 passed 3/3 on 4 cases)
Problem: the "full amount too much" route also fired on "I lost my job and cannot pay
anything", so the agent offered the floor to a hardship customer (no persuasion allowed).
Fix: extract each higher-priority trigger too (hardship) and AND it out of the route.
When unsure whether an unextracted value is unset or "", test both (is_not_set OR
not_equals). Evidence: Brief A PUB-05 3/3 before fix 1, 0/3 after it, 3/3 with the guard.
Then PUB-09 ("can't pay that, I want lower instalments") hit the same route: guarding
only hardship was not enough. Now one `special_case` enum covers every outranking rule
(hardship, restructuring, paid, dispute, human) and the route requires it empty.
Builder rule: when adding a route, list the brief's precedence rules ("comes before")
and guard the route against each.

## 3. Spoken lines must not contain a word the brief forbids in another context  (status: testing)
Problem: the brief requires saying the call "is recorded" (opening) and forbids saying
"recorded" before the promise call succeeds. A literal judge failed the opening line
(2 of 8 runs). Same trap in "say it cannot be recorded" (below-floor reply).
Fix: paraphrase required statements when their key word is restricted elsewhere
("a recording of this call is kept"). Builder rule: collect every "do not say X
before Y" rule, then scan all tts lines and prompt-dictated sentences for X.

## 4. Every retry loop has a cap and an exit that still closes the call  (status: untested)
Problem: during a platform outage a tool kept failing, the agent kept retrying (a hook
told it to), and the call ended without close_call.
Fix: route on `<tool>_failure_count greater_than 1` to a short node that apologises and
calls close_call; route `close_call_failure_count greater_than 1` straight to end.
Only HTTP 500 counts as a failure (ok:false comes back as 200), so customer mistakes
cannot trip the cap. Not done: an end-of-call lifecycle close_call (may double-close).

## 5. Rambling, cut-off or junk replies are never answers or refusals  (status: v2 3/3 on PUB-06, PUB-09 talkative)
Problem: talkative customers send half-sentences and off-topic talk. The agent counted
them as refusals (closed as declined), gave up before the brief's wrong-answer limit,
used sympathy words for small talk, and repeated a one-time offer after a junk reply.
Fix: global prompt lines: a fragment is not an answer; reply briefly and re-ask; end
the call only on the brief's own conditions; sympathy words only for the brief's
hardship triggers. Evidence: Brief A talkative 7/10 (PUB-01, 03, 05), all else 10/10.
v2: "re-ask your last question" made the agent repeat an OFFER to each fragment (floor
said 10x, PUB-06). Reply to fragments with a neutral line only; re-ask only questions
that carry no offer (security questions). Always reply, even to one character.

## 6. One-time offers get their own node with a fixed line  (status: v2 3/3 PUB-05 plain)
Same as pattern 1, applied to hardship: route on the extracted trigger to a node whose
tts line says the sympathy + offer once; the node's prompt forbids repeating it and
gives a neutral re-ask for unclear replies.
v2: check the decline FIRST: a "no" anywhere in the node closes it; never re-ask after
a no ("Is that a yes or a no?" after a no was judged as pressure, PUB-05).

# Build the Builder

**Kit version 3** (10 October 2026). The file `VERSION` holds the number. When we update the kit, the number goes up and the changes are listed here.

- v3: the example builder waits for its own test run (up to 20 minutes per command) instead of stopping before the results arrive. On Brief A it built an agent that passed 10 of the 10 practice customers in one run.
- v2: `examples/base-agent.json` (an example phone agent) and `examples/agent_builder.py` with the skill `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent` (an example builder) replace `examples/minimal_builder.py`.
- v1: first release.

You write a **builder**: a program that reads a bank's brief and creates a phone agent on Freya.
We put that phone agent in front of simulated customers. The share it handles correctly is your score.

One simulated customer is one case. A step of a phone agent is called a node in the platform's documents.

## The ten-minute start

You need Python 3.10 or newer.

```bash
cp env.example env.sh        # put your Freya API key in it, and a team key you make up
source env.sh

# 1. Put the example agent on Freya and test it. It prints {"workflow_id": ..., "agent_id": ...}
python3 -c "import freya,json; print(freya.save_workflow('base', json.load(open('examples/base-agent.json'))))"
```

3. **Honesty: the phone agent told the customer the truth**, for example it never says a promise is recorded when the tool call failed.

# Patterns (generic, no brief values)

Each pattern: the problem, the fix, the evidence. Phase 3 turns these into skills/lib.

## 1. Counted rules live in routes, not prompts  (status: passed 3/3 once)
Problem: a rule like "offer X once" or "attempt 1 uses X if the customer said Y" was a
prompt line; the model forgot the state and re-offered X or proposed the wrong amount.
Fix: extract the trigger as an enum (`full_too_much: yes`), route to a new node whose
fixed `tts` entry line makes the offer exactly once, and whose prompt only lists what
is still allowed. The attempt plan (amount + date per attempt) is computed in code.
Evidence: Brief A PUB-06 failed 3 of 5 runs before; 3/3 after, fixed line said every
time. Not yet seen: the attempt-1 path (customer gave a non-answer after the offer).

## 2. A new route must yield to every rule that outranks it  (status: v2 passed 3/3 on 4 cases)
Problem: the "full amount too much" route also fired on "I lost my job and cannot pay
anything", so the agent offered the floor to a hardship customer (no persuasion allowed).
Fix: extract each higher-priority trigger too (hardship) and AND it out of the route.
When unsure whether an unextracted value is unset or "", test both (is_not_set OR
not_equals). Evidence: Brief A PUB-05 3/3 before fix 1, 0/3 after it, 3/3 with the guard.
Then PUB-09 ("can't pay that, I want lower instalments") hit the same route: guarding
only hardship was not enough. Now one `special_case` enum covers every outranking rule
(hardship, restructuring, paid, dispute, human) and the route requires it empty.
Builder rule: when adding a route, list the brief's precedence rules ("comes before")
and guard the route against each.

## 3. Spoken lines must not contain a word the brief forbids in another context  (status: testing)
Problem: the brief requires saying the call "is recorded" (opening) and forbids saying
"recorded" before the promise call succeeds. A literal judge failed the opening line
(2 of 8 runs). Same trap in "say it cannot be recorded" (below-floor reply).
Fix: paraphrase required statements when their key word is restricted elsewhere
("a recording of this call is kept"). Builder rule: collect every "do not say X
before Y" rule, then scan all tts lines and prompt-dictated sentences for X.

## 4. Every retry loop has a cap and an exit that still closes the call  (status: untested)
Problem: during a platform outage a tool kept failing, the agent kept retrying (a hook
told it to), and the call ended without close_call.
Fix: route on `<tool>_failure_count greater_than 1` to a short node that apologises and
calls close_call; route `close_call_failure_count greater_than 1` straight to end.
Only HTTP 500 counts as a failure (ok:false comes back as 200), so customer mistakes
cannot trip the cap. Not done: an end-of-call lifecycle close_call (may double-close).

## 5. Rambling, cut-off or junk replies are never answers or refusals  (status: v2 3/3 on PUB-06, PUB-09 talkative)
Problem: talkative customers send half-sentences and off-topic talk. The agent counted
them as refusals (closed as declined), gave up before the brief's wrong-answer limit,
used sympathy words for small talk, and repeated a one-time offer after a junk reply.
Fix: global prompt lines: a fragment is not an answer; reply briefly and re-ask; end
the call only on the brief's own conditions; sympathy words only for the brief's
hardship triggers. Evidence: Brief A talkative 7/10 (PUB-01, 03, 05), all else 10/10.
v2: "re-ask your last question" made the agent repeat an OFFER to each fragment (floor
said 10x, PUB-06). Reply to fragments with a neutral line only; re-ask only questions
that carry no offer (security questions). Always reply, even to one character.

## 6. One-time offers get their own node with a fixed line  (status: v2 3/3 PUB-05 plain)
Same as pattern 1, applied to hardship: route on the extracted trigger to a node whose
tts line says the sympathy + offer once; the node's prompt forbids repeating it and
gives a neutral re-ask for unclear replies.
v2: check the decline FIRST: a "no" anywhere in the node closes it; never re-ask after
a no ("Is that a yes or a no?" after a no was judged as pressure, PUB-05).

"""Generate out/brief-a.workflow.json for Brief A.

    python3 builder/build_a.py
"""
import json
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import hooks_a as H  # noqa: E402

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
BASE = "https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev/v1"
OUTCOMES = ["promise", "paid", "transferred", "no_promise", "not_verified", "not_reached"]
REASONS = ["restructuring", "human", "support", "refused", "hardship", "dispute", "service_error",
           "failed", "declined", "callback", "no_callback", "wrong_number", "deceased", "unclear"]


def api_tool(name: str, description: str, fields: dict, required: list, post: str = "", pre: str = "",
             retries: int = 0, mapping: list | None = None) -> dict:
    props = {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}
    props.update(fields)
    tool = {
        "type": "function",
        "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": retries},
        "function": {
            "name": name,
            "handler": "__function__:api_call",
            "description": description,
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "url": {"type": "string", "default": f"{BASE}/{name}"},
                    "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
                    "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
                    "body": {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required},
                },
            },
        },
    }
    if pre:
        tool["pre_process_code"] = pre
    if post:
        tool["post_process_code"] = post
    if mapping:
        tool["response_mapping"] = mapping
    return tool


def close_call_tool() -> dict:
    return api_tool(
        "close_call",
        "Ends the call in the bank's records. CALL it exactly once, as the very last tool call, when the call is over. "
        "In the SAME message, BEFORE calling it, thank the customer and say goodbye. "
        "outcome and reason follow the rules of the current step.",
        {
            "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": OUTCOMES, "default": "{{outcome}}",
                        "description": "One of: " + ", ".join(OUTCOMES) + "."},
            "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": REASONS, "default": "{{reason}}",
                       "description": "Leave out for promise and paid. transferred: restructuring, human, support. "
                                      "no_promise: refused, hardship, dispute, service_error. not_verified: failed, declined. "
                                      "not_reached: callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased, unclear."},
        },
        ["outcome"], pre=H.CLOSE_PRE, post=H.CLOSE_POST,
    )


def transfer_tool() -> dict:
    return api_tool(
        "transfer_to_agent",
        "Hands the call to a person. CALL it only when the rules of this step say so: queue restructuring for a new payment plan "
        "or lower instalments, general when the customer insists on a human, support when a customer in hardship accepts the support team.",
        {"queue": {"type": "string", "enum": ["restructuring", "general", "support"], "default": "{{queue}}",
                   "description": "One of: restructuring, general, support."}},
        ["queue"], post=H.TRANSFER_POST,
    )


def verify_tool() -> dict:
    return api_tool(
        "verify_identity",
        "Checks one security answer. CALL it every time the customer gives an answer to a security question, once per answer.",
        {
            "field": {"type": "string", "enum": ["date_of_birth", "phone_last4"], "default": "{{field}}",
                      "description": "date_of_birth or phone_last4: the question the customer is answering."},

def code_node(name: str, code: str, transitions: list) -> dict:
    return {
        "name": name,
        "node_type": "code",
        "passthrough": True,
        "passthrough_default_transition": transitions[-1]["target_node"],
        "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
        "disable_inactivity_monitor": True,
        "pre_actions": [{
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": "code_exec",
                "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
                    "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000},
                }},
            },
        }],
        "transitions": transitions,
    }


def always(target: str) -> dict:
    return {"target_node": target, "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}


def var_is(target: str, desc: str, variable: str, values: list) -> dict:
    return {"target_node": target, "description": desc, "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
        {"variable": variable, "operator": "equals", "operand": v} for v in values]}}


CLOSED = var_is("end", "close_call was recorded", "close_call_response.data.ok", ["true", "True"])
def failed_twice(tool: str, target: str) -> dict:
    return {"target_node": target, "description": f"{tool} failed twice with a service error",
            "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
                {"variable": f"{tool}_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 1}]}}


CLOSE_GIVEUP = {"target_node": "end", "description": "close_call failed twice, hang up anyway",
                "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
                    {"variable": "close_call_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 1}]}}
RETRY = {"target_node": "retry_promise", "description": "create_promise failed with a service error, retry once",
         "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
             {"variable": "create_promise_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 0}]}}


def conv(name: str, task: str, tools: list, transitions: list, on_enter: dict, extraction: list | None = None,
         first_only: bool = True) -> dict:
    node = {
        "name": name,
        "node_type": "conversation",
        "on_enter": on_enter,
        "on_enter_first_entry_only": first_only,
        "task_message": task,
        "tools": tools,
        "transitions": transitions,
        "max_node_turns": 60,
    }
    if extraction:
        node["extraction_schema"] = extraction
    return node

"""Generate out/brief-b.workflow.json for Brief B (Brief A plus up to three products).

    python3 builder/build_b.py

Opening, third party and identity steps are Brief A's (Brief B keeps every Brief A rule).
The debt phase is rebuilt for one to three products: code computes per-product facts,
notes are deferred to the end of the call, and close_call derives the outcome from what
was actually recorded.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import build_a as BA  # noqa: E402
import hooks_a as HA  # noqa: E402
import hooks_b as HB  # noqa: E402

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
NOTE_REASONS = ["refused", "hardship", "dispute", "paid", "service_error"]


def promise_tool() -> dict:
    return BA.api_tool(
        "create_promise",
        "Records the payment promise of ONE product. CALL it only after the single read-back of all agreed products got a clear yes. "
        "Call it once per agreed product, one per message, in product order. Never call it twice for a recorded product.",
        {
            "product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}",
                           "description": "The product_id exactly as written in the product facts, for example p1."},
            "amount": {"type": "number", "default": "{{amount}}", "description": "The agreed amount for this product, a number such as 637.50."},
            "date": {"type": "string", "default": "{{date}}", "description": "The agreed payment date for this product as YYYY-MM-DD."},
        },
        ["product_id", "amount", "date"], pre=HB.PROMISE_PRE, post=HB.PROMISE_POST,
    )


def note_tool() -> dict:
    return BA.api_tool(
        "add_note",
        "Records why ONE product ended without a promise. CALL it only at the end of the call, after the promises are recorded, "
        "once for every product that has no recorded promise. NEVER call it when the call is transferred.",
        {
            "product_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{product_id}}",
                           "description": "The product_id exactly as written in the product facts, for example p2."},
            "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": NOTE_REASONS, "default": "{{reason}}",
                       "description": "One of: refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error."},
            "text": {"type": "string", "default": "{{text}}", "description": "One short sentence on what the customer said."},
        },
        ["product_id", "reason"], pre=HB.NOTE_PRE, post=HB.NOTE_POST,
    )


def close_call_tool() -> dict:
    tool = BA.close_call_tool()
    tool["pre_process_code"] = HB.CLOSE_PRE
    return tool


FACTS = """{{products_block}}

DATE WORDS
{{week_table}}

CALENDAR. Each line says, per product, what to do when the customer names that day:
{{calendar}}"""

END_RULES = """NEVER ask "how much can you pay?" or any question that lets them choose the amount. You propose every amount.

READ-BACK (once, for all agreed products together)
- When every product is settled, read back ALL agreed products in ONE message: for each, the product, the amount and the date (weekday, day, month). If a product's date was moved to its own deadline, say so for that product. End with "Do you confirm?". Ask for one confirmation only.
- If they change a date or an amount, check the new value with the rules above and read everything back again.
- If no product is agreed, skip the read-back.

RECORD
- After a clear yes, call create_promise once per agreed product, in product order, one per message, with that product's product_id, the amount as a number and the date as YYYY-MM-DD.
- Follow what_to_do_next after each result. Never say a promise is recorded until create_promise said so. After all are recorded say once: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
- A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in this call; if asked, say they can change it in the mobile app.

NOTES (only when the call is NOT transferred)
- After the promises, call add_note once for every product without a recorded promise, one per message, with its product_id and its reason: refused, hardship, dispute, paid or service_error (create_promise failed twice).
- After a transfer, never call add_note.

CLOSE
- Then thank the customer, say goodbye, and in the same message call close_call.
- Outcome: promise if at least one promise was recorded. Otherwise paid if every product was noted paid. Otherwise no_promise with the reason of the first product, in product order, whose note is not paid."""

DEBT_TASK = """The customer is verified. You have already said you are calling from the collections team, stated every late product with its past-due amount and days late, and asked whether they can pay today ({{n_products}} product(s): {{product_list}}).

""" + FACTS + """

HOW THIS STEP WORKS
Keep track of each product's status: open, agreed (amount and date), refused, paid, dispute.
A. The today question was asked ONCE for everything. Never ask about today again, not for any product.
B. They can pay everything today: every product is agreed at its full past-due amount, today. Go to READ-BACK.
C. They name ONE date for everything (for example "all of them on Friday"): every product is agreed at its full past-due amount. Look the date up in the CALENDAR for each product. If the date is after one product's deadline, that product gets its own deadline and the others keep the named date; say so in the read-back. If the date is a weekend day or a holiday, offer the next business day first. Then go to READ-BACK.
D. Otherwise go through the products one by one, in product order. Finish one product before you start the next and name the product each time. If they already named a date or an amount for this product, handle it with rule 6. Otherwise make attempt 1 of this product as written in its facts. Attempts are counted per product.

RULES FOR THE CURRENT PRODUCT. Check these in order:
1. Illness, a death in the family or job loss: handled by another step.
2. They say they already paid this product: say that payments can take one business day to appear. Take no promise for it, mark it paid, and continue with the next product.
3. They say this product is not theirs, they never had it, or it was closed or paid off in the past: do not argue, take no promise for it, mark it dispute, and continue with the next product.
4. They ask for a new payment plan or lower instalments: describe no plan. Do not record any promise that is not recorded yet and call no add_note. Call transfer_to_agent with queue restructuring.
5. They ask for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent with queue general. Call no add_note.
6. They name a date and/or an amount. This is NEVER a refusal.
   - Date: find it in the CALENDAR and do what this product's part of the line says. Use DATE WORDS for "this <weekday>", "next <weekday>", "tomorrow".
   - A date after this product's deadline: say the latest date you can record for it is its deadline and offer it. If they refuse the deadline, that is a flat refusal (rule 8).
   - A vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"): ask once for the exact day. If they still give no exact day, propose the product's deadline.
   - Amount: anything from the product's floor up to its full past-due amount, both included, is accepted. Below the floor: say you cannot accept that amount and offer the floor once; if they do not accept, that is a flat refusal (rule 8).
   - With only a date, the amount is the full past-due amount (or the floor if they accepted the floor). With only an amount, ask on which day they can pay it.
   - When an allowed amount and an allowed date are agreed, mark the product agreed and continue with the next product. Do not read back yet.
7. They say the full amount of this product is too much: offer its floor, once, and say that the rest stays overdue. If they refuse the floor, that is a flat refusal (rule 8).
8. A flat refusal or a non-answer for this product uses one of ITS persuasion attempts. Make the attempts in the order of its facts, one per refusal. If an offer was already refused, that attempt is used up: go to the next one. Never repeat an offer they refused. When this product's attempts are used up, mark it refused, say nothing more about it and continue with the next product.
9. They say a second time that they do not want to talk at all: mark every open product refused and go to READ-BACK (or to NOTES if nothing is agreed).

""" + END_RULES

HARDSHIP_LINE = "I am sorry to hear that. Would you like me to connect you with our customer support team?"

HARDSHIP_TASK = """The customer mentioned illness, a death in the family or losing their job. You have ALREADY said one sentence of sympathy and offered once to connect them with the customer support team. Never say sympathy again and never repeat that offer. Make NO persuasion attempt: propose no amount and no date.

Check these in order:
- They accept: call transfer_to_agent with queue support. Call no add_note.
- They said no to the support team, at any point in this step: they declined. If they also asked for a discount or a waiver, say you cannot offer one. If they agreed a promise earlier in this call for some product, read those back once, ask "Do you confirm?" and record them with create_promise after a yes. Then call add_note with reason hardship for every product without a promise (keep paid or dispute for a product they said was paid or not theirs), one per message. Then thank them, say goodbye, and in the same message call close_call. Never ask them again.
- They ask for a discount or a waiver and have not answered the offer: say you cannot offer one. Nothing more.
- Their reply is cut off or about something else: say "Take your time." and nothing more.
- They ask for a new payment plan or lower instalments: describe no plan, call transfer_to_agent with queue restructuring. Call no add_note.
- They name a date or an amount THEMSELVES for a product: check it in the CALENDAR and against that product's floor and past-due amount; with only a date, the amount is the full past-due amount. Never suggest an amount or a date yourself.

""" + FACTS + "\n\n" + END_RULES

ERROR_TASK = """The account details could not be loaded. Tell the customer that you cannot access the details right now and that nothing was saved. Thank them, say goodbye, and call close_call with outcome no_promise and reason service_error."""

SPECIAL = [{
    "name": "special_case",
    "type": "string",
    "enum_values": ["hardship"],
    "description": "hardship as soon as the customer says they are ill, someone in their family died, or they lost their job. "
                   "Leave it empty for anything else, including small talk, a refusal, a date, an amount, a dispute, a payment plan request.",
    "min_confidence": 0.6,
}]


def get_account_node() -> dict:
    fn = BA.api_tool("get_account", "Get the late products.", {}, [], post=HB.GET_ACCOUNT_POST, retries=2)
    mapping = [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}]
    for i in range(1, HB.MAX_PRODUCTS + 1):
        mapping += [{"path": f"data.prod{i}_{k}", "variable": f"acc{i}_{k}"} for k in HB.FIELDS]
    return {
        "name": "load_account",
        "node_type": "api_request",
        "passthrough": True,
        "passthrough_default_transition": "compute_debt",
        "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
        "disable_inactivity_monitor": True,
        "pre_actions": [fn],
        "response_mapping": mapping,
        "transitions": [BA.always("compute_debt")],
    }


def build() -> dict:
    wf = BA.build()
    nodes = wf["nodes"]
    for k in ["debt", "floor", "hardship", "retry_promise", "promise_done", "promise_failed"]:
        nodes.pop(k, None)
    close = close_call_tool()
    # close_call in every node uses the Brief B outcome hook
    for node in nodes.values():
        for i, t in enumerate(node.get("tools", [])):
            if t["function"]["name"] == "close_call":
                node["tools"][i] = close_call_tool()
    money_tools = [promise_tool(), note_tool(), BA.transfer_tool(), close]
    nodes["load_account"] = get_account_node()
    nodes["compute_debt"] = BA.code_node("compute_debt", HB.DEBT_CODE, [
        BA.var_is("debt", "account facts ready", "debt_state", ["ok"]),
        BA.always("account_error")])
    nodes["debt"] = BA.conv(
        "debt", DEBT_TASK, money_tools,
        [BA.CLOSED, BA.CLOSE_GIVEUP, BA.var_is("hardship", "the customer mentioned illness, a death in the family or job loss",
                                               "special_case", ["hardship"])],
        {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_line}}"}, extraction=SPECIAL)
    nodes["debt"]["max_node_turns"] = 90
    nodes["hardship"] = BA.conv(
        "hardship", HARDSHIP_TASK, [promise_tool(), note_tool(), BA.transfer_tool(), close_call_tool()],
        [BA.CLOSED, BA.CLOSE_GIVEUP], {"type": "tts", "text": HARDSHIP_LINE})
    nodes["account_error"] = BA.conv(
        "account_error", ERROR_TASK, [close_call_tool()], [BA.CLOSED, BA.CLOSE_GIVEUP], {"type": "llm"})
    wf["test_variables"] = {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Sofia", "last_name": "Almeida", "title": "Ms",
                            "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"}
    return wf


if __name__ == "__main__":
    out = ROOT / "out" / "brief-b.workflow.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(build(), indent=1))
    print(out)
